core_obligations: For part (1), cut Z out by the product of the ideal sheaves, note that Z cap U splits, apply the separation lemma over Z, and show the resulting blowup of the center Y on X is U-admissible with the same strict transforms (proof lines 9568-9605).
For part (2), write the constructible closed subsets as zero loci of finite type ideals on U, extend them to X, and invoke part (1) (proof lines 9593-9605).
proof_roadmap: Part (1): the product ideal and the blowup on Z (proof lines 9568-9579).
Part (1): lifting the blowup to X and comparing strict transforms (proof lines 9581-9605).
Part (2): reduction to part (1) via extension of ideals (proof lines 9593-9605).
difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated X with a quasi-compact open U, the lemma asserts that closed subschemes Z_1, Z_2 of finite presentation whose intersection with U is empty can be made to have disjoint strict transforms by a U-admissible blowup, and that disjoint constructible closed subsets T_1, T_2 of U can be separated in the same way (statement lines 9553-9566). For part (1) the proof notes that finite presentation of Z_i means the ideal sheaves I_i are of finite type by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, forms Z cut out by the product I_1 I_2, observes that Z cap U is the disjoint union of Z_1 cap U and Z_2 cap U, and applies Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-separate-disjoint-opens-by-blowing-up to get a (U cap Z)-admissible blowup Z' -> Z with disjoint strict transforms (proof lines 9568-9579). If Y is the center of that blowup, then Y -> X is a closed immersion of finite presentation by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-composition-finite-presentation, so the blowing up X' -> X of Y is U-admissible, and the strict transforms of Z_1 and Z_2 with respect to X' -> X agree with those with respect to Z' -> Z by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-strict-transform (proof lines 9581-9605 in part (1), and the same computation gives part (1)). For part (2) one writes each T_i as V(J_i) for a finite type ideal J_i on U by Properties, Lemma labelled properties-lemma-quasi-coherent-finite-type-ideals, extends J_i to a finite type ideal I_i on X by Properties, Lemma labelled properties-lemma-extend, and applies part (1) to Z_i = V(I_i) (proof lines 9593-9605). Reproducing the blowup on Z as a blowup on X so that the strict transforms agree is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
